findings.finding: Issued April 26, 2017; FR publication May 1. Secretary to review qualifying designations from 1996; consider enumerated criteria, consult federal and affected officials as appropriate. Separate, one-time reports with recommendations to President through OMB director, Assistants for Economic and Domestic Policy and CEQ chair. Interim covers Bears Ears and any others chosen; final summarizes review (not just other sites). 45 and 120 elapsed calendar days yield June 10 and August 24, not self-executing performance or expiration. Section 1 states policy; §3 preserves lawful authority, OMB functions, appropriation limits, and disclaims enforceable rights.

findings.basis: final PDF pp.3,9; DOI Hammond House testimony, Jan 30 2018, Background
findings.finding: Report identified and dated June 10, 2017 in final memo; memo attributes concrete tribal co-management recommendation to interim. Hammond states the Secretary submitted two reports for Presidential consideration and identifies first as Bears Ears interim. Held sources support submission by time of testimony; date of document alone does not fix day of submission or of receipt.

External interim memorandum, addressed to the President, self-identifies as §2(d) report; recommends modifying boundary and seeking congressional action. Dated June 12 agency announcement expressly states it was submitted to President on Saturday June 10, 2017. Thus exact Secretary-side submission, on computed due date. The date of the press announcement differs from that of submission. No dated Presidential receipt or each intermediary’s transmission shown.

Final reports work: named terrestrial and marine monuments (hearing: 27), public comment through July 10, site visits/official and stakeholder meetings, and joint marine review with Commerce. Recommending Secretaries of Commerce/Agriculture concurred on specified recommendations (p.10). Supports actual examination/consultation, not verified completion of every criterion, consultation, or other agency’s parallel duties.

Rendered p.1 shows a signed-looking Zinke memorandum for the President, without dateline. P.2 states August 24 as deadline, not performance. P.3 expressly identifies this as §2(e) Final Report. P.10 reports that recommendations have been submitted to President. P.18 conditions later separate specific measures on concurrence. P.20 shows four cc entries matching specified offices; mailing/receipt/routing log absent. File creation/modification metadata concerns scanning, not legal timing.

findings.basis: agency_release_b p.1; agency_answers response 88–89, printed p.42; testimony Background; final PDF pp.6,10
findings.finding: DOI described a draft with findings and recommendations sent August 24, 2017. QFR distinguishes that draft from public release of final December 5, 2017. Signed-looking final exists; public release fixes existence by December 5. Hearing retrospectively affirms final report among two reports submitted to President by January 30, 2018. Public release not Presidential delivery. No exact final submission day, no logged receipt day, no byte identity between the August submission and the December public copy. July 10 close of comment discussed in the memo is a content-based lower bound (no earlier than July 10) for production of this substantive final; April 26–January 30 is a conservative outer envelope for reported final submission. Late vs timely delivery not decided; August 24 draft is not proof no final could also have been sent then.

Secretary-side one-off acts of submitting two reports supported. Do not read the order as requiring President to accept recommendations or perform boundary changes; do not require proof of Presidential reading as a condition absent textual basis. No direct proof of every step through the named chain or completion date of all review activity. December 4, 2017 presidential proclamations modified Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante; independent instruments, not effects accomplished by the reports themselves. Proposals to Congress and ongoing DOI management planning are not §2(d)/(e) reporting duties. No first whole-order exhaustion date inferred. January 20, 2021: EO 13990 §7(a) expressly revokes 13792 without exception; §3 launches a separate review with its own report, and §7(f) directs appropriate follow-up rescission steps rather than automatically unwinding every implementation. Revocation establishes a historical end as an authority, not prior nonperformance or automatic elimination of downstream instruments. No present-status or no-revival claim through project cutoff.

residuals: Exact final transmittal day, any version identity or change between draft and submitted final, date/sequence of each intermediary, White House receipt/acknowledgment; not disproved by missing receipts. Seek dated White House/DOI correspondence, version identifiers and through-route logs.

Independent verification of all review/consultation elements; completion of contingent implementation or legislative requests; whole-order first ending or later monument history through cutoff; not adjudicated here.
